text: (Theorem, so a test of my code.) At each of the 1,460 times the number of pairs is odd.
The median number of pairs is 7; at 90 % of the times it lies between 3 and 13; it is 1 at fewer than 2 % of the times.

At least 70 % of all pairs have their points within 40 degrees of the equator, because temperature is nearly symmetric about the equator and the curve "same temperature as the antipode" should stay at low latitudes.
Fewer than 5 % of pairs have both points over land; more than half have both over sea.
From one field to the next (six hours) the count changes at fewer than half of the steps, and when it changes it changes by exactly 2 in at least 80 % of those cases.
Molecules that contain sulfur are less pleasant than the rest by at least 8 points on the 100-point scale.
Of the 20 molecules rated most "garlic", at least 10 contain sulfur.
Of the 10 molecules rated most "fish", at least 5 contain nitrogen.
Familiarity and pleasantness go together: correlation at least 0.4.
Strength and pleasantness barely go together: correlation between -0.3 and 0.3.
Larger molecules are somewhat more pleasant: correlation of size with pleasantness between 0.1 and 0.5.
Larger molecules smell weaker: correlation of size with strength at most -0.2.
Agreement between people: median 0.35 to 0.70 for strength, 0.25 to 0.55 for pleasantness, and higher for strength than for pleasantness.
Vanillin or ethyl vanillin is among the 10 most pleasant molecules (void if neither is in the set). Of the 10 least pleasant, at least 6 contain sulfur or are acids.
The model predicts pleasantness with a correlation between 0.45 and 0.70, strength between 0.35 and 0.70, and "garlic" at 0.5 or more.
At 900 m the best rotation has its pole within 6 degrees of 44.0 N, 30.6 W and its angle within 3 degrees of 57.0.
The misfit there is between 40 and 130 km.
The shelf edge fits better than the coast: the misfit at 900 m is at least 20 % smaller than at the coastline.
Of 200, 500, 900, 2000 and 3000 m, the smallest misfit is at 900 or 2000 m.
Where the two continents overlap most, it is at the Niger delta (built out since they parted): the largest overlap lies within 600 km of 4.5 N, 6 E.
Bullard's own rotation, applied to these margins, has a misfit no more than 25 % above that of my best one.
For being sure of the title the two always agree (the worst case, the leader losing everything and one rival winning everything, is always possible): lead 0 in all ten seasons. A test of my program.
Out of the title: the exact date is earlier than the simple one in between 20 % and 60 % of the 190 team-seasons that do not win; the largest lead is between 0.5 and 4 rounds.
Safe: exact earlier than simple in between 20 % and 60 % of the team-seasons that end up safe.
Doomed: exact earlier than simple for at least 5 of the 30 relegated teams, and never by more than 2 rounds.
Sure of the top four: exact earlier than simple for at least 10 of the 40.
Nowhere is the lead more than 5 rounds.
The rule finds between 8 and 11 terminations in 800,000 years.
Their tilt phases are clustered: R is 0.5 or more, and evenly spread phases do as well less than 5 % of the time.
The mean tilt phase lies between 240 and 30 degrees: that is, from a third of a cycle before the tilt's maximum to just after it (the tilt rising or high).
Precession phases are less clustered than tilt phases (smaller R).
At least 5 of the intervals between successive terminations lie within 12,000 years of 82,000 or 123,000 years (two or three tilt cycles).
Burlington's mayoral election of 2009 (from memory): the Condorcet winner is Andy Montroll, the plurality winner is Kurt Wright, and instant runoff elects Bob Kiss.
A Condorcet winner exists in at least 97 % of the elections.
Where one exists, the plurality winner is that candidate in between 85 % and 97 % of elections.
Where one exists, instant runoff elects that candidate in at least 95 % of elections; it fails at least once (Burlington) and at most five times.
In the elections where the plurality winner is not the Condorcet winner, instant runoff elects the Condorcet winner in at least 70 % of them.
The typical first flowering (median of all records) lies between day 50 and day 70 of the year (19 February to 11 March).
It has moved earlier: the mean of 1991-2020 is earlier than the mean of 1961-1990 by between 7 and 20 days.

Winter warmth explains it: the yearly figure correlates with Germany's mean January-February temperature more strongly than -0.7, and a degree of warmth brings flowering forward by between 4 and 9 days.
Altitude: between 2 and 4.5 days later per 100 m (Hopkins: 3.3).
Latitude: between 1 and 5 days later per degree northward (Hopkins: 4).
Longitude: between 0.5 and 3 days later per degree eastward (Hopkins: 0.8).
Years differ a great deal: the standard deviation of the yearly figure is between 8 and 16 days, and the earliest year is at least 30 days ahead of the latest.
For every c the walkers' detour is below 1 / sqrt(1 - c^2) (a walker held at the largest allowed angle to the line of sight walks a logarithmic spiral of exactly that relative length).
L falls steadily as c grows: within 5 % of 3 at c = 0.1, below 2.2 at c = 0.8.
For c up to 0.7 the systems are nearly efficient: D exceeds the line's value at the same L by less than 0.04.
At c = 0.9 it is more than 0.2 above the line.

A full Y (no inner triangle left: the three arms meet within 0.05 of the centre) appears first at c = 0.8 or 0.9, not before: the arm of a Y turns a walker 60 degrees from the line of sight at the centre, and sin 60 = 0.87.
On the two boards, agent3 has written the most words, agent2 the second most, agent1 the fewest, and agent1 less than 15 % of the total.
Function words alone, files: between 0.45 and 0.65.
All words, files: 0.85 or more.
Punctuation and shape alone do at least as well as function words alone.
Trained on files and tested on board posts of 100 words or more (function words): above chance but below K2's figure; between 0.38 and 0.55.
Of the three, agent2 (I) has the highest rate of semicolons and the lowest rate of em dashes in the files.
A permutation test (author labels shuffled among projects) puts the function-word score of K2 beyond the 99th percentile of chance.
The number of pairs is odd at every time, at stride 1, 2 and 5.
At stride 5 (a 5-degree grid) the mean count over the year is between 20.5 and 30.7 (NCEP/NCAR 2025 on its 5-degree grid: 25.6).
The mean count at stride 1 (1 degree) is between 2.5 and 4.5 times the mean count at stride 5. (If the count went on growing like (grid step)^-0.7 the ratio would be 3.1.)
The mean count at stride 2 is between 1.6 and 2.2 times that at stride 5 (the power law gives 1.9).
At stride 1, July and August are the two months with the lowest mean count, April is among the three highest, and the twelve monthly means correlate with those of NCEP/NCAR 2025 at 0.8 or more.
The number of pairs is odd at each of the 1,464 times.
The mean number of pairs over the year is between 31 and 38 (2025: 34.6).

July and August are the two months with the lowest mean count. April and November are both among the three months with the highest. The correlation between the twelve monthly means of 2024 and those of 2025 is at least 0.9.
Of the four hours, 06 UTC has the lowest mean count and 00 UTC the highest (2025: 30.4 and 37.9).
The fewest pairs at any time of the year is 3 or 5, and it falls in July, August or September.
The number of pairs is odd at every time and every stride.
At stride 10 (2.5 degrees) the mean count is between 1.0 and 1.6 times the NCEP/NCAR mean on the same times (34.7), and the two counts correlate across the times at 0.6 or more.
The mean count at 0.25 degrees is between 1.2 and 2.2 times the mean count at 1 degree (stride 4).
The share of pairs with at least one end on land is higher at 0.25 degrees than at 2.5 degrees (stride 10) by at least 5 percentage points: the pairs that a finer grid adds come from terrain.
The mean count at 0.25 degrees is between 50 and 150.
Three-way, little words and punctuation together: 0.70 or more.
Every pair of the three is separated at 0.75 or more.
With pieces joined to at least 1,200 words, three-way: 0.85 or more.
The readers do better than the little-words method: pooled three-way score above 0.49.
The pooled three-way score is between 0.55 and 0.80.
Between Noon and Yonder alone (pieces by those two, answers other than those two counted wrong): between 0.65 and 0.85.
Asked what they went by, at least two of the three readers will name the subject matter or kind of work (mathematics against experiment or checking) before any habit of style.
